subject: [Escalation] Live adapter: intermittent payload-gap causing 5xx / throughput collapse
messages:
From: Simon Keller <simon.keller@checkoutco.com>
To: ops@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: nina.park@checkoutco.com
Date: 2028-10-03T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: Checkout live pipeline seeing 5xx, huge p99 latency spike

Hi team —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and p99 latency in our Checkout live stream at ~08:50 PDT. Affected flows are the payment-confirmation path that uses the streaming adapter (long-lived connection). Throughput dropped by ~40% and many requests end with a connection reset.

Quick details:
- Affected region: us-west-2
- Error symptom: connection reset / 502 / occasional 504s; end-to-end throughput drop
- We've attached a short PCAP showing repeated zero-length trailer frames before connections close (pcap_excerpt).

This needs urgent attention — this is impacting our holiday promotion traffic. Please escalate to engineering and let us know mitigation steps.

Thanks,
Simon
Head of Platform Ops, CheckoutCo
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Simon Keller <simon.keller@checkoutco.com>, ops@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-03T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Checkout live pipeline seeing 5xx, huge p99 latency spike

Simon — thanks for the alert and PCAP. I'm triaging now and have looped in our live-streaming and SDK teams.

Immediate actions we are taking:
- Triage runbook triggered and we've opened JIRA-INC-8742.
- Rolling a short-lived routing rule to force CheckoutCo traffic off streaming adapter to the polling endpoint (non-streaming) as a mitigation; this will reduce throughput pressure while we investigate.
- Asking CheckoutCo to increase client-side timeout to 90s if possible (temporary).

Can you confirm any recent SDK upgrades on your side in the last 24–48 hours? Also attaching the PCAP snippet we received.

I'll update within 30 minutes with root-cause hypothesis and next steps.

— Vivek
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-03T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Checkout live pipeline seeing 5xx, huge p99 latency spike

Quick triage note (initial findings):

- Reproduced locally with a synthetic client that mirrors CheckoutCo's adapter: when server emits small trailer headers after a zero-length chunk, our JS/Go SDK dechunker sometimes ignores the trailer boundary. The result: the HTTP/2 stream remains open but subsequent frames are misaligned, leading to the parser returning an EOF+protocol error upstream -> connection reset.
- This pattern shows up under high concurrency and small-chunk streaming (common in short-response interactive use cases).
- We have a test failing consistently when we force a trailer-without-length edge-case (attached stacktrace).

Root-cause hypothesis: an off-by-one in the dechunker state machine that drops an intermediate empty-chunk delimiter when chunk metadata is present. That causes the next header frame to be interpreted as payload and triggers a parse error.

Immediate mitigation:
1) Hotfix branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/compare/fix/stream-dechunker (PR #1327).
2) Canary the hotfix on a small subset of CheckoutCo traffic (will coordinate with Vivek).
3) Add conservative server-side guard: detect malformed trailer sequences and gracefully reject with 400 instead of letting parser abort the connection (short-term).

I'll send a patch in the next 25 minutes.

— Jonas
Principal SWE, Realtime
From: Nina Park <nina.park@checkoutco.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: simon.keller@checkoutco.com
Date: 2028-10-03T10:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Checkout live pipeline seeing 5xx, huge p99 latency spike

Thanks Vivek and Jonas — we did a config change yesterday to enable the new adapter performance flags (sdk v2.4.0). We can roll back if that helps, but we'd prefer a targeted fix.

We're standing by on the canary and can keep traffic diverted to polling for 2–4 hours. We also need a customer-facing summary for our ops and exec teams.

— Nina
SRE Lead, CheckoutCo
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: Checkout live pipeline seeing 5xx, huge p99 latency spike

Patch and rollout plan:

- PR #1327 contains a corrected dechunker state transition and adds test vectors that were previously missing. Attached: hotfix-pr-diff.patch (diff summary).
- Canary plan: 5% CheckoutCo traffic to the patched runtime + SDK handshake, monitor for 15 minutes, then 25%, then 100% if stable.
- Fallback: if canary fails, roll back and keep routing to polling endpoint until full fix is validated.
- Additional instrumentation: increase sampling for stream parser traces and add metric for dropped-delimiter events.

Exec note: this is a codepath exercised by several high-volume customers; recommend a cross-team communication to Sales/CS and an exec briefing in 60–90 minutes (looping in Marissa for the customer comms).

— Jonas
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: simon.keller@checkoutco.com, nina.park@checkoutco.com
Date: 2028-10-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem summary & exec next-steps: CheckoutCo live adapter incident

Summary (TL;DR):
- Impact: CheckoutCo saw a ~40% drop in streaming throughput and elevated 5xxs between 08:50–11:30 PDT. Customer traffic routed to polling endpoint at 09:00; canary of fix started 10:55; full rollout completed 11:25; observed stabilization by 11:30.
- Root cause: client SDK/server dechunker mismatch — an off-by-one state transition that drops zero-length chunk delimiters when trailer metadata is present. Under load this resulted in parser misalignment and connection resets.
- Mitigations taken: emergency routing to polling endpoint, SDK hotfix PR #1327, canary -> full rollout, server guard added to return graceful 400s for malformed trailers.
- Customer impact: CheckoutCo had elevated error rates for ~2.5 hours; they diverted traffic and leadership requested a credit evaluation.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- SDK: backport fix to stable v2.x branch and publish patch (Aditya / 48h).
- Instrumentation: add dropped-delimiter metric and dashboard (Dylan / 72h).
- E2E tests: add streaming trailer edgecases to CI (Jonas / 7d).
- Customer communications: coordinate credit + exec note (Marissa / 24h).
- Post-mortem doc: full RCA and timeline (Vivek / 72h).

Attached: pcap excerpt, stacktrace log, PR diff.

Marissa — can you draft the customer email/credit proposal? I'll join the 1pm CET exec sync.

— Vivek
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
